Dr Rafiqur Rahman with MA Baqui Ismail and Sirajur Rahman, Advocates ----- For the Appellant. 
MA Wahab with AK Shamsuddin, Advocates ----- For the Respondents
parties:
Manager, Bangladesh Krishi Bank and others ------ Defendant-Appellants 
vs 
Al-Haj Md Nurul Islam & another ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Abdul Matin J: This appeal at the instance of the defendants is directed against the judgment and decree dated 19-1-1994 passed by the Subordinate Judge Munshiganj in Money Suit No. 1 of 1991. 

 2. The Respondent as plaintiff instituted Money Suit No. 1 of 1991 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Munshiganj against the defendant-appellants for a decree of Taka 87,75,000.00 as damage. The plaintiff in the suit is Alhaj Muhammad Nurul [slam, Managing Director, Jamal Ice and Cold Storage Limited, Registered Office No. 14 Bijoy Nagar, PS Motijheel, District Dhaka and the defendants are the Manager, Regional Manager and Managing Director of Bangladesh Krishi Bank. The plaintiff is a private limited company and the defendants are the officials of a Bank which is the creature of President's Order 27 of 1972. 

 4. The defence case as per written statement is that on the prayer of the plaintiff company Bangladesh Krishi Bank granted loan to the plaintiff as per condition contained in the Annexure to the sanction letter and against DP Note. letter of acceptance, letter of continuity, revival letter etc, and against mortgagee deed subsequently registered in favour of the Bank but in gross violation of those conditions the company did not pay the installments and compelled the Bank to file Artha Rin Adalat Case No. 1 of 1991 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Munshiganj for the decree of Taka 1,71,64,336.00 and the suit was decreed against the plaintiff company on 21-3-92 for Taka 89,88,000.00 only. The further case of the defendants Bank as per written statement is that the plaintiff's suit was not maintainable and was liable to be dismissed. 

 5. The trial Court decreed the suit for Taka 49,71,250.00. 

 6. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree of the learned Subordinate Judge, the defendant preferred this appeal. 

 8. The learned Advocate appearing for the appellants submits that the judgment and decree by the Court below are based on no evidence and absolutely on hunch, surmise and conjecture. The learned Advocate further submits that the very issue whether due to the activities of the Bank plaintiff suffered loss or not was very much an issue in Artha Rin Adalat Case No. 1 of 1991 of the Court of Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Munshiganj and after framing proper issue on this point the allegation of the defendants in that suit was rejected and that suit was decreed and as such the subsequent suit is hit by section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure in view of the findings already given in Artha Rin Adalat Case No. 1 of 1991 which was decreed as early as on 21-3-1992 by a Court of competent jurisdiction between the same parties having the matter substantially in issue between them. 

 9. The learned Advocate further submits that the Bangladesh Krishi Bank from whom admittedly the plaintiff sought damage is not a party in this suit and as such the suit was not maintainable and decree if any passed by the Court will not be executable against Bangladesh Krishi Bank and it is not executable against the defendants who are only the employees of the Bank. 

 10. Mr MA Wahab, the learned Advocate appearing for the respondent submits that the trial Court correctly decreed the suit considering the laches on the part of the Bank. He further submits that although Bangladesh Krishi Bank is not a party in the suit but the concerned Branch Manager, Bangladesh Krishi Bank, Beyalia Branch, Betake and Regional Manager, Krishi Bank, Munshiganj and even the Managing Director of Bangladesh Krishi Bank are very much parties in this suit and that for the non-implication of the Krishi Bank as defendant it cannot be said that the suit is not maintainable. The learned Advocate further submits that the suit i.e. Artha Rin Adalat Suit No. 1 of 1991 and Money Suit No. 1 of 1991 are of different nature and decided by Judges under different jurisdiction and therefore the question of res judicata does not arise. 

 11. Both the Advocates for the appellants and the respondent have taken us through the paper book. We have considered the deposition of PW 1 and DW 1 and the Exhibits. There are certain things which are admitted in this appeal. Firstly the plaintiff respondent admittedly took loan and failed to repay the installments for which Artha Rin Suit No. 1 of 1991 was filed against the plaintiff company and decreed on 21-3-1992 against which First Appeal No. 86 of 1992 was preferred by the Bank and the appeal has been allowed by this Court maintaining the decree in respect of principal amount and only modifying the rate of interest from the date of institution of the suit till realisation. 

 19. Now coming to the question of res judicata, Mr Wahab could not deny that in the earlier suit it was Bangladesh Krishi Bank that was the plaintiff and it was the plaintiff respondent who was the defendant. He could not deny that the Bank claimed 1,71,64,336.00 and the suit was decreed for Taka 89,88,000.00. He further could not deny that in issue Nos. 4 and 5 in the earlier suit the defendants' case of damage done to the cold storage due to failure of the Bank to pay adequate loan, timely in stalemates, non-co-operation in collecting loan from other Bank and non-collecting the claim of the Insurance company were considered by the Court and defence case was not accepted and the suit was decreed in favour of plaintiff of that suit. It is not denied that the Artha Rin Suit was filed on 13-1-1991 whereas the present suit i.e.. Money suit No. 1 of 1991 was filed on 17-8-1991 and thus admitted position is that the present suit is a subsequent suit. It is also admitted that the earlier suit was decreed on 21-3-1992 by the Subordinate Judge, Munshiganj and Artha Rin Adalat Munshiganj whereas the present suit was decreed by the Subordinate Judge Munshiganj on 21-1-1994 though not as Artha Rin Adalat but as Civil Court. If further appears that the written statement filed in Artha Rin Adalat Suit No. 1 of 1991 by the plaintiff company in their capacities as defendant in that suit is in substance the plaint of the subsequent Money Suit No. 1 of 1991. Thus we find that the parties and the subject matter in both the suits are the same and the matter in issue as to the loss sustained by the plaintiff due to the reasons stated in the written statement of the earlier suit and plaint of the subsequent suit are materially and substantially the same and these issues were raised in the earlier suit and by necessary implication was rejected in the earlier suit and that decree of the trial Court has already been affirmed by this Court in First Appeal No. 86 of 1992. 

 "7. Mr MH Khandker, the learned Counsel appearing for the plaintiffs-appellants, canvassed that the earlier suit was of mere declaration of title whereas the instant suit is for declaration of title and recovery of possession and further the earlier suit was dismissed in the absence of any prayer for recovery of possession and as such the decree in that suit does not operate as res judicata in the present suit. This point has no substance. Section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure clearly comes into play and explanation-IV is to the following terms: 

 23. In the case of Sachindra Lal Das and others vs Hriday Ranjan Das being dead his heirs: Bimal Kanti Das and others reported in 40 DLR (AD) 56, it was held that if the adverse finding is actually the decision of the suit and forms a fundamental part of the decree, then it will operate as res judicata. But adverse finding interlocutory order will not operate as res judicata, if made incidentally. 

 25. In the instant case the question whether the plaintiff company suffered any loss or not due to laches, non-co-operation or activities of the Bank was considered and rejected in the earlier suit and that suit was decreed against them and those adverse finding in the earlier suit do necessarily form the basis of res judicata in the subsequent suit. 

 26. On the question of maintainability the learned Advocate for the appellant has referred two unreported case of (1) Md Arfan Ali vs Sonali Bank and other passed in Civil petition for leave to Appeal No. 26 of 1992 and (2) Mohammad Abdul Naim vs Chairman, Board of Director Sonali Bank, Head Office and others passed in civil Petition for leave to Appeal No. 298 of 1994 where the question was in absence of Sonali Bank whether a decree against its employees are executable and whether such cases are maintainable in absence of the Bank. In the facts and circumstances of those cases it was held that although the petitioner before the Administrative Tribunal was appointed by the defendants and appeal was also dismissed by the appellate authority who are also employees of the Bank but nonetheless the plaintiff was not in the service of those officers and any decree against those officers of the Bank cannot be executable against the Bank itself because Sonali Bank is a juristic person. 

 In view of the findings as above we find substance in this appeal and accordingly this appeal is allowed and the impugned Judgment and decree passed in Money Suit No. 1 of 1991 are hereby set aside and Money Suit No. 1 of 1991 of the Court of Subordinate Judge, Munshiganj in dismissed.
